stages.title: Functional Requirements
stages.questionPrompt: What are the core functional requirements for this system?
stages.howToAnswer: List 3-5 'Users should be able to...' statements covering the must-have behavior. Skip nice-to-haves and admin features unless explicitly asked.

should: REPLACE — extra capability that strengthens the answer
avoid: REPLACE — common drift trap (e.g., dashboards, accounts when not asked)

stages.title: Non-Functional Requirements
stages.questionPrompt: What are the non-functional requirements for this system?
stages.howToAnswer: Cover availability vs consistency, latency targets with concrete numbers, scale (DAU/QPS/storage), durability. Tie each requirement to a real product concern.

must: REPLACE — the headline NFR (e.g., uniqueness, durability, no-double-booking)

stages.sampleAnswer:
- REPLACE first NFR with concrete number.
- REPLACE second.
- REPLACE third.

stages.title: Core Entities
stages.questionPrompt: What are the core entities of this system?
stages.howToAnswer: List the nouns. Don't define schemas yet — that comes in High-Level Design.

avoid: Inventing entities the requirements don't justify

stages.sampleAnswer:
- EntityA: REPLACE one-line description.
- EntityB: REPLACE.

stages.title: API
stages.howToAnswer: One endpoint per functional requirement. REST is the default — show method, path, request body shape, and response.

avoid: Putting body data in the URL path

stages.title: High-Level Design
stages.questionPrompt: Sketch the high-level architecture. Walk through each endpoint.
stages.howToAnswer: Boxes and arrows: client → load balancer → API service → database. Note schema fields next to the database. Walk through each endpoint end-to-end.

must: Client / Load balancer / API service / Database
REPLACE the design's headline trick (e.g., short-code generation, dispatch algorithm)

stages.sampleAnswer: REPLACE: walk through write path then read path. Mention the headline trick. Show component boundaries.

stages.title: Deep Dives
stages.questionPrompt: Harden the design against the non-functional requirements.
stages.howToAnswer: Pick 2-3 of the highest-risk areas given the NFRs and address each with a concrete mechanism.

must: REPLACE biggest risk (e.g., scaling reads, ID-generation bottleneck)
avoid: Adding components without a justifying NFR
